description: This grouped bar chart illustrates the "Average Change Using Compression" across various levels of "Observation Probability." The horizontal category axis is labeled "Observation Probability" and displays five discrete numerical categories in ascending order: 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9. The vertical value axis is labeled "Average Change Using Compression" and uses a linear scale ranging from -3 to 2, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 1. For each observation probability category, the chart displays a group of two vertical bars. According to the legend located below the chart, the grey bars positioned on the left of each group represent "Inferred Frames," while the light yellow bars on the right correspond to a second category whose text label is obscured by a grey rectangle. The grey bars representing Inferred Frames consistently display negative values across all categories, with the largest negative magnitude of approximately -2.9 at an observation probability of 0.2, and the smallest negative magnitude of approximately -1.2 at 0.9. Conversely, the light yellow bars primarily display positive values, except for a slight negative value of approximately -0.1 at the 0.2 category. The tallest light yellow bar reaches a maximum value of approximately 2.0 at an observation probability of 0.5, with the remaining positive bars at 0.4, 0.7, and 0.9 showing approximate values of 0.9, 1.4, and 1.5, respectively. The categories on the horizontal axis are sorted numerically, and the chart features a light grey background grid with no specific bars visually emphasized.
